The {{convert|6|ft|10|in|adj=on}} [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] from Melbourne previously attended [[Box Hill Senior Secondary College]] and [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]], and has represented the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]]. Simmons has been touted as a possible [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web | last=Payten | first=Iain | url=http://www.news.com.au/sport/more-sports/australian-ben-simmons-is-expected-to-be-the-nbas-next-big-thing/story-fndukor0-1227484037039 | title=Australian Ben Simmons is expected to be the NBA’s ‘next big thing’ | work=News.com.au | date=14 August 2015 | accessdate=15 August 2015}} ==Early life== Simmons was born in the [[Melbourne]] suburb of [[Fitzroy, Victoria|Fitzroy]], to American father [[Dave Simmons (basketball, born 1963)|Dave]] and Australian mother Julie. When his parents met in 1991, Julie was a divorced single mother with four children—Melissa, Emily, Liam and Sean. After their marriage in 1994, they added Olivia and Ben to their family. Even though the six children have two different biological fathers, and their age span is 15 years (Melissa to Ben), they were raised as if they were full siblings.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/14050003/from-melbourne-baton-rouge-ben-simmons-arrived-lsu |title=From Melbourne to Baton Rouge, Ben Simmons has arrived at LSU |first=Dana |last=O'Neil |work=ESPN.com |date=5 November 2015 |accessdate=5 November 2015}}{{cite web | url=http://www.wsucougars.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30400&ATCLID=208211954 | title=Emily Tribe Profile | work=WSUCougars.com | accessdate=24 November 2014}} Dave is a [[Melbourne United|Melbourne Tigers]] legend who came to the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] from the United States in 1989 after playing college basketball for [[Oklahoma City Stars men's basketball|Oklahoma City University]].{{cite web | last=Auerbach | first=Nicole | url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2015/06/19/ben-simmons-lsu-basketball-nba-guard-forward-recruit/71257494/ | title=LSU's versatile Ben Simmons has a natural position: Star | work=USAToday.com | date=19 June 2015 | accessdate=20 June 2015}} Simmons was raised in [[Newcastle, New South Wales|Newcastle]] from the age of 18 months while his father played and coached in the city. Simmons played his first year of basketball at the age of seven in the Newcastle Hunters' under-12 representative team and played two more years for Lake Macquarie and Newcastle.{{cite web | last=Keeble | first=Brett | url=http://www.theherald.com.au/story/1874183/boomers-boss-sees-something-special-in-simmons/ | title=Boomers boss sees something special in Simmons | work=TheHerald.com.au | date=29 October 2013 | accessdate=30 November 2014}} While in Newcastle, he also played junior [[rugby league]] for the [[Western Suburbs Rosellas|Western Suburbs]] and [[South Newcastle Lions|South Newcastle]] in the [[Newcastle Rugby League|local competition]].{{cite web | last=Keeble | first=Brett | url=http://www.theherald.com.au/story/1843236/basketballer-ben-simmons-high-hopes-for-nba-video/ | title=Basketballer Ben Simmons high hopes for NBA: video | work=TheHerald.com.au | date=15 October 2013 | accessdate=24 November 2014}} At the age of 10, Simmons returned to Melbourne with his family and began playing junior basketball for the [[Knox Basketball Inc|Knox Raiders]].{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=194803351&client=1-8876-125585-204983-16780515 | title=Player statistics for Ben Simmons – BVDL | work=FoxSportsPulse.com | accessdate=24 November 2014}} Along with basketball, he also played [[Australian rules football]] at the junior level for the Beverley Hills Junior Football Club and won a number of team and league [[Best and Fairest]] awards. At the age of 14, Simmons was torn between his two sporting loves of basketball and Australian rules football, but eventually decided to focus on basketball.{{cite web | last=Sygall | first=David | url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/the-hype-around-louisiana-state-university-star-ben-simmons-is-warranted-but-its-a-long-way-to-the-top-if-you-want-to-pick-and-roll-20150815-gizs4d.html | title=The hype around Louisiana State University star Ben Simmons is warranted, but it's a long way to the top if you want to pick and roll | work=SMH.com.au | date=15 August 2015 | accessdate=17 November 2015}}{{cite web | last=Walker | first=Rod | url=http://www.aussiehoopla.com/lsu-signee-ben-simmons-good-advertised | title=LSU SIGNEE BEN SIMMONS AS GOOD AS ADVERTISED | work=AussieHoopla.com | accessdate=17 November 2015}}{{cite web | last=Calle | first=Franklyn | url=http://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/features/ben-simmons-slam-feature/ | title=Long Way Home | work=SlamOnline.com | date=10 November 2014 | accessdate=25 November 2014}} Simmons later revealed it was his football coach's decision to play him in the position of [[Ruckman (Australian rules football)|ruckman]] that swayed his decision to pursue basketball. The following year in grade 9, at the age of 15, he played basketball for [[Box Hill Senior Secondary College]] at the 2011 Australian Schools Championships before taking up a scholarship at the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in 2012.{{cite web | last=Bernard | first=Grantley | url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/this-son-of-a-gun-has-a-very-big-future/story-e6frf9if-1226205378198 | title=This son of a gun has a very big future | work=HeraldSun.com.au | date=25 November 2011 | accessdate=24 November 2014}} Later that year, despite still being 15 years of age, he was chosen to represent [[Australia national under-17 basketball team|Australia]] at the [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] and helped his team win the silver medal. Simmons' tournament highlights included a 26-point, 10-rebound, 5-steal outing against the Czech Republic.{{cite web | url=http://kaunas2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/fu17wc/men/p/eid/6228/ct/0/gid/8/grid/A/rid/9024/sid/6228/game.html | title=Boxscore: Czech Republic 58-63 Australia 01 July 2012 | work=FIBA.com | accessdate=17 November 2015}} ==High school career== ===Sophomore year=== In January 2013, Simmons moved to [[Montverde, Florida]], to attend [[Montverde Academy]], where he immediately started playing for them. In April 2013, he helped Montverde rally from a 16-point deficit to beat New Jersey's St Benedict's 67–65 in the final of the High School National Tournament. After competing in the Jordan Brand Classic International Game,{{cite web | last=Bortoluzzi | first=Davide | url=http://www.nbadraft.net/2013-jordan-brand-classic-international-prospects | title=2013 Jordan Brand Classic: International Prospects | work=NBADraft.net | date=17 April 2013 | accessdate=29 March 2015}} he returned to Melbourne where he joined the Bulleen Boomers of the [[Big V]] competition in June 2013.{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/assoc_page.cgi?c=1-4600-0-0-0&sID=127406&news_task=DETAIL&articleID=24115173 | title=Big V Round 12 – Men's Teams on a Roll | work=FoxSportsPulse.com | date=16 June 2013 | accessdate=24 November 2014}} He managed six games for Bulleen while averaging 12.3 points, 8.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists, 1.3 steals and 2.3 blocks per game.{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=197568188&client=1-7930-99134-253030-18677653 | title=Player statistics for Ben Simmons – Big V | work=FoxSportsPulse.com | accessdate=15 August 2015}} ===Junior year=== Simmons returned to Montverde Academy for his junior season in 2013–14. On the season, Simmons averaged 18.5 points, 9.8 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game while shooting 69 percent from the field and 77 percent from the free throw line. He recorded 88 blocks as well. Montverde finished the season with a 28–0 record, closing with a 71–62 victory over Oak Hill Academy in the High School National Tournament at Madison Square Garden. Simmons had 24 points and 12 rebounds as he earned MVP honours.{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=27826&SPID=2166&ATCLID=209763114 | title=Men's Basketball Signs Nation's No. 1 Player | work=LSUSports.net | date=12 November 2014 | accessdate=24 November 2014}}{{cite web | last=Hustwaite | first=Megan | url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/leader/east/nba-draft-hopeful-ben-simmons-heads-back-to-box-hill-senior-secondary-college/story-fngnvmqa-1226957200341 | title=NBA draft hopeful Ben Simmons heads back to Box Hill Senior Secondary College | work=HeraldSun.com.au | date=17 June 2014 | accessdate=24 November 2014}} Following the season, he was named America's top high school junior and was voted MVP at the National Basketball Players' Association Top 100 camp.{{cite web | last=Keeble | first=Brett | url=http://www.theherald.com.au/story/2386842/basketball-junior-ben-simmons-has-world-at-his-big-feet/ | title=Basketball junior Ben Simmons has world at his big feet | work=TheHerald.com.au | date=30 June 2014 | accessdate=20 August 2015}} ===Senior year=== [[File:20150401 MCDAAG Ben Simmons posts Ivan Rabb (2).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Simmons in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] On 12 November 2014, Simmons signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for [[Louisiana State University]]. On 28 January 2015, Simmons was named in the East team to compete in the 38th annual [[McDonald's All-American Game]].{{cite web | last=Borzello | first=Jeff | url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12243846/mcdonald-all-american-game-rosters-unveiled | title=East, West rosters unveiled | work=ESPN.com | date=28 January 2015 | accessdate=23 February 2015}}{{cite web | last=Adaimy | first=Roje | url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/allamerican-honour-for-australian-boomers-young-gun-ben-simmons-20150129-1313rl.html | title=All-American honour for Australian Boomers young gun Ben Simmons | work=SMH.com.au | date=29 January 2015 | accessdate=23 February 2015}} On 10 March 2015, he was named the Morgan Wootten Award winner, given annually to the best male McDonald's All-American player who exemplifies outstanding character, exhibits leadership and embodies the values of being a student-athlete in the classroom and in the community. In doing so, he became just the second player from a Florida high school to win the award behind [[Austin Rivers]] in 2011.{{cite web | last=Biancardi | first=Paul | url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12453568/ben-simmons-no-1-college-basketball-recruit-wins-morgan-wootten-award | title=Ben Simmons wins Wootten Award | work=ESPN.com | date=10 March 2015 | accessdate=10 March 2015}} He was then named the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] on 12 March{{cite web | last=Borzello | first=Jeff | url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12468896/ben-simmons-named-naismith-trophy-boy-high-school-player-year | title=Ben Simmons wins Naismith Trophy | work=ESPN.com | date=12 March 2015 | accessdate=20 March 2015}} and the [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] on 24 March after leading the Eagles to a 28–1 record and a berth in the High School National Tournament for the third straight year.{{cite web | last=Konecky | first=Chad | url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/ben-simmons-wins-gatorade-national-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year | title=Ben Simmons wins Gatorade National Boys Basketball Player of the Year | work=usatodayhss.com | date=24 March 2015 | accessdate=24 March 2015}} In 29 regular season games, he averaged 28.0 points, 11.9 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 2.6 steals per game while shooting 70.7 percent from the field and recording 24 double-doubles. After competing in the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]] on 1 April, Simmons led Montverde Academy to a third consecutive High School National Tournament title with a 70–61 win over Oak Hill Academy on 4 April at Madison Square Garden. He again earned MVP honours after recording 58 points and 35 rebounds over the three-day tournament.{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/video/clip?id=12618204 | title=Montverde Academy wins third straight national title | work=ESPN.com | date=5 April 2015 | accessdate=5 April 2015}}{{cite web | url=http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2015/04/05/simmons-3rd-us-school-basketball-title | title=Simmons' 3rd US school basketball title | work=SBS.com.au | date=5 April 2015 | accessdate=5 April 2015}} He then competed in the 2015 [[Nike Hoop Summit]] for the World Team on 11 April and scored 13 points in a 103–101 win over Team USA.{{cite web | last=Vecenie | first=Sam | url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/25145366/world-team-beats-usa-in-nike-hoop-summit-behind-murrays-30 | title=World Team beats USA in Nike Hoop Summit behind Murray's 30 | work=CBSSports.com | date=11 April 2015 | accessdate=12 April 2015}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Simmons was listed as the No. 1 power forward and the No. 1 player in the nation in 2015.{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/166633/ben-simmons | title=Ben Simmons – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles | work=ESPN.com | accessdate=26 April 2015}} ==College career== Entering his freshman year of college, Simmons began his career in Australia on a four-stop national tour with the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers men's basketball team]]. Relishing the opportunity to show his teammates where it all began for him,{{cite web | last=Dinjaski | first=Melanie | url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/us-sports/aussie-basketball-phenom-ben-simmons-adjusting-to-crazy-college-life-at-lsu/story-e6frf6ju-1227487819142 | title=Aussie basketball phenom Ben Simmons adjusting to ‘crazy’ college life at LSU | work=FoxSports.com.au | date=18 August 2015 | accessdate=18 August 2015}} Simmons made his debut for LSU on 15 August in an 89–75 win over the Newcastle All-Stars in the first game of LSU's preseason Australia trip. His double-double of 22 points and 10 rebounds led the way for the Tigers, playing at the [[Broadmeadow Basketball Stadium|Newcastle Basketball Stadium]] where his father played professionally for the [[Newcastle Falcons (basketball)|Newcastle Falcons]] in the late 1990s.{{cite web | last=Payne | first=Terrence | url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/08/15/ben-simmons-records-double-double-in-first-game-for-lsu/ | title=Ben Simmons records double-double in first game for LSU | work=NBCSports.com | date=15 August 2015 | accessdate=18 August 2015}} The Tigers completed their five-game Australian tour with a 3–2 record, and over the five games, Simmons averaged 20 points and nine rebounds per game to lead the team in all major statistical categories.{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/pdf9/3733006.pdf?ATCLID=210284787&SPSID=27826&SPID=2166&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=5200 | title=LSU Combined Team Statistics (as of Aug 22, 2015) | work=LSUSports.net | accessdate=31 August 2015}}{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=210284787 | title=Basketball Tour Ends as Melbourne Turns Tables | work=LSUSports.net | date=22 August 2015 | accessdate=31 August 2015}} Upon returning to the United States, Simmons was featured on the [[Blue Ribbon College Basketball Yearbook]] 35th anniversary cover,{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=210297412 | title=Simmons on 'Blue Ribbon' Preseason All-America Team | work=LSUSports.net | date=27 August 2015 | accessdate=31 August 2015}} was named the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]]'s Preseason Player of the Year,{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=210438088 | title=Simmons Named SEC Preseason Player of the Year | work=LSUSports.net | date=21 October 2015 | accessdate=21 October 2015}} and earned Associated Press preseason All-America team honours.{{cite web | url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/ben-simmons-named-to-ap-preseason-all-america-team-just-fourth-freshman-to-get-nod/story-e6frf3f3-1227602548060 | title=Ben Simmons named to AP preseason All-America team - just fourth freshman to get nod | work=FoxSports.com.au | date=10 November 2015 | accessdate=11 November 2015}} His Preseason Player of the Year honour made him just the second freshman to earn the award, joining Kentucky's [[Julius Randle]] in 2013, and his All-America team honour made him just the fourth freshman to be honoured on the preseason team. On 13 November 2015, Simmons made his college debut in LSU's season opener, recording a double-double with 11 points and 13 rebounds as a starter in a win over [[McNeese State Cowboys basketball|McNeese State]].{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=210496600 | title=Freshmen Pace Basketball Past McNeese, 81-70 | work=LSUSports.net | date=13 November 2015 | accessdate=13 November 2015}} He helped LSU start the season 3–0 before recording 21 points, 20 rebounds, 7 assists and 2 steals in a loss to [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] on 23 November.{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400827731 | title=Marquette uses late free throws to nip No. 22 LSU 81-80 | work=ESPN.com | date=23 November 2015 | accessdate=24 November 2015}} On 2 December, he helped LSU break a three-game losing streak by recording 43 points, 14 rebounds, 7 assists, 5 steals and 3 blocks in a 119–108 win over [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida]]. His 43 points were the most for a Tigers player since [[Shaquille O'Neal]] had 43 against [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball|Northern Arizona]] on 28 December 1991.{{cite web | url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400830776 | title=Ben Simmons matches Shaq as LSU rallies, outlasts North Florida | work=ESPN.com | date=2 December 2015 | accessdate=3 December 2015}} After recording 14 points and 10 rebounds in a win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] on 5 January 2016, Simmons was dubbed the best all-round player since [[LeBron James]] by NBA Hall of Famer [[Magic Johnson]].{{cite web | url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-01-06/ben-simmons-the-best-all-round-player-since-lebron-magic/7070708 | title=Ben Simmons the best all-round player since Lebron James: Magic Johnson | work=ABC.net.au | date=6 January 2016 | accessdate=6 January 2016}} On 11 February, he was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]].{{cite news|last=Payne|first=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=19 February 2016|work=FoxSports.com|date=11 February 2016}} Nine days later, Simmons came off the bench for the first time after being removed from LSU's starting line-up for their game against [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] due to academic reasons.{{cite news|title=Ben Simmons benched by Louisiana State for academic reasons|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/ben-simmons-benched-by-louisiana-state-for-academic-reasons-20160221-gmzja0.html|accessdate=21 February 2016|work=SMH.com.au|date=21 February 2016}} Following the conclusion of the regular season, Simmons was named first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference]] and the league's [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|Freshman of the Year]] on the 2016 Coaches SEC voting. He was also named to the eight-player All-SEC Freshman team.{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=210783388 | title=Blakeney, Simmons Named to All-SEC Teams | work=LSUSports.net | date=8 March 2016 | accessdate=11 March 2016}} As the fourth seed in the [[2016 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|2016 SEC Tournament]], Simmons helped LSU (18–13) defeat Tennessee in the quarter-finals to move on to the semi-finals where they faced first-seeded [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]]. LSU bowed out of the tournament with a demoralising 71–38 loss to the Aggies, as Simmons was unsuccessful in leading the Tigers to an NCAA tournament berth.{{cite web | last=Franchuk | first=Jason | url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2624202-what-went-wrong-for-ben-simmons-lsu-after-ncaa-tourney-hopes-end | title=What Went Wrong for Ben Simmons, LSU After NCAA Tourney Hopes End? | work=BleacherReport.com | date=12 March 2016 | accessdate=13 March 2016}} Simmons completed the 2015–16 season having played in 33 games with 32 starts. He led the team in all major statistical categories except three-point and free throw shooting, finishing with averages of 19.2 points, 11.8 rebounds, 4.8 assists, 2.0 steals and 0.8 blocks in 34.9 minutes per game, while shooting 56.0% from the field, 33.3% from three-point range and 67.0% from the free throw line.{{cite web | url=http://www.lsusports.net/fls/5200/assets/docs/mb/16stats/teamcume.htm | title=2015–16 LSU Men's Basketball Season Statistics | work=LSUSports.net | accessdate=13 March 2016}} Following the announcement of the NCAA tournament field, with LSU failing to earn a bid, Tigers head coach [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]] announced that the team would not play in any postseason tournament. On 21 March 2016, Simmons declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.{{cite url|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/15032022/ben-simmons-lsu-tigers-enter-nba-draft |title=Ben Simmons to enter NBA draft |first=John |last=Goodman |work=ESPN.com |date=21 March 2016 |accessdate=21 March 2016}} He withdrew from school at the conclusion of the season with plans to move immediately to [[Phoenix, Arizona]] in advance of the NBA draft.{{cite url|url=http://theadvocate.com/sports/latestsports/15256887-129/espn-report-lsus-ben-simmons-declaring-for-nba-draft |title=LSU’s Ben Simmons withdraws from school to enter NBA draft; father says hiring agent 'shouldn't be far off' |first=Sheldon |last=Mickles |work=TheAdvocate.com |date=21 March 2016 |accessdate=21 March 2016}} He also signed with American sports agency Klutch Sports, which is primarily owned by [[Rich Paul]].{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/basketball/ben-simmons-set-to-cash-in-with-lebron-james-agency-before-nba-debut-20160314-gnix02.html |title=Ben Simmons set to cash in with LeBron James' agency before NBA debut |first=Peter |last=Mitchell |work=SMH.com.au |date=15 March 2016 |accessdate=17 March 2016}}{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nba/ben-simmons-signs-with-klutch-sports-group-what-comes-next-after-linking-with-nba-superagent/news-story/8a93ce0408c737130b543c281d15110b |title=Ben team|LSU]] | 33 || 32 || 34.9 || .560 || .333 || .670 || 11.8 || 4.8 || 2.0 || .8 || 19.2 |- {{S-end}} ==Professional career== In the week leading up to the [[2016 NBA draft]], Simmons' attitude and character were questioned by a number of NBA media analysts.{{cite news|url=http://www.news.com.au/sport/american-sports/76ers-coach-untroubled-by-negativity-surrounding-ben-simmons-attitude/news-story/b1230c150d2f82868a426b53c347835b |title=76ers coach untroubled by Australian national team coach and a friend of the Simmons family, retorted the claims being made and was content with Simmons' pre-draft behaviour. ==National team career== After participating in the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian Boomers]] camp ahead of the Sino-Australia Challenge in June 2013, Simmons went on to make his senior debut for Australia in the [[2013 FIBA Oceania Championship]] against [[New Zealand national basketball team|New Zealand]], a month after his 17th birthday. He subsequently scored four total points in the two-game series.{{cite web | url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/98944/pid2//sid/6589/tid/239/tid2//_/2013_FIBA_Oceania_Championship_for_Men/index.html | title=Ben Simmons's profile | work=FIBA.com | accessdate=24 November 2014}} In July 2014, Simmons was named in the Boomers extended squad for the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].{{cite web |
